To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the perceptual approach is still the best way to evaluate voice disorders, but it requires a lot of training; 2) the objective approach can be useful to support the perceptual approach, but it is not a replacement for it; 3) automatic speaker recognition techniques may provide an interesting alternative to the perceptual approach.

(1) the best voice quality assessment system combines perceptual and acoustic information; (2) automatic voice quality assessment is possible and can be used to complement perceptual assessment; (3) the best automatic assessment method relies on a combination of several acoustic measurements; and (4) the best acoustic measurement is a nonlinear combination of several acoustic parameters.

(i) the combination of several acoustic measurements provides a better classification of voice samples than any single measurement, (ii) the ASR approach is a promising alternative to the classical approach for the automatic evaluation of pathological voice.

the development of complementary approaches for the assessment of voice quality and their integration in a common framework.
the development of complementary approaches to voice quality assessment.
the development of a new voice quality assessment method based on the integration of the complementary approaches of acoustic measurement and percept.

a good knowledge of voice mechanisms and their perceptual correlates is necessary in order to build a good voice quality evaluation system, but that the use of complementary approaches is also a good strategy to overcome the limitations of a single approach.
